messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each city with appropriate facilities. The function expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to pass an array for Cafe? Actually the type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That means facilities can be one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? Wait the type is ambiguous. It might mean facilities can be either a string from the set or an array of "Cafe". But likely they want to pass an array of strings? The description: "Facilities and sections in public library." So we should pass an array of strings like ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc. But the type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; maybe they want to pass an array of strings. Let's interpret as array of strings. We'll pass array of strings for each query.

So we need to call function thrice:

1. location: "New York, NY" facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA" facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL" facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to call the function for each. The function returns any. We'll call it thrice. Use the function tool.
